Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Our infra team wants a short mutual action plan (MAP) that includes concrete perf targets and access instructions so we can validate latency/throughput and TTFT at 100 and 500 concurrent sessions.

High-level asks from Acme Health:
- p50/p95 latency under typical payloads (mean token length ~120)
- steady-state throughput at 100 and 500 concurrent streams
- time-to-first-token (TTFT) under cold and warm cache
- validation runbook and required test accounts/keys

We can carve out a 4-hour window next week (prefer mornings PST). Ben from LoadLab is copied — he will drive load generation. Please include a schedule and a logistics checklist in the MAP so we can sign off and close.

Best,
Eva
Eva Stone
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Eva Stone <eva.stone@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@loadlab.io>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance verification and MAP kickoff

Eva — thanks, great summary. Attaching a short MAP (MAP_AcmeHealth_v3.pdf) and a load script template (load_script_v2.jmx) for LoadLab. High level plan below and in the attached MAP.

MAP summary (milestones):
1) Logistics & access (Target: 2026-06-29) — grant test API keys, whitelist test IPs, confirm dataset/seed prompts
2) Pre-tests (Target: 2026-06-30 morning) — small-scale warmup, KV cache priming, baseline latency swimlane
3) Validation runs (Target: 2026-06-30 10:00–14:00 PST) — staged ramp to 100 concurrent, steady 30m; ramp to 500 concurrent, steady 30m
4) Results consolidation (Target: 2026-06-30 evening) — metrics export + CSV attached (results_20260630.csv)
5) Close & next steps (Target: 2026-07-01) — finalize SLA language and production cutover timeline

Perf targets (we propose):
- p50 latency (generation token cadence): < 180 ms at 100 concurrency; < 240 ms at 500 concurrency
- p95 latency: < 400 ms at 100 concurrency; < 800 ms at 500 concurrency
- Throughput: ability to sustain 120 tok/s per GPU node (target aggregated throughput for your model profile in MAP)
- TTFT: cold < 900 ms; warm < 220 ms (measured from request to first byte)

Logistics checklist (short):
- Provide test API key (scoped, rate-limited) and whitelist LoadLab IPs
- Confirm model variant and tokenization params + sample prompt set (we asked for your 20 prompts)
- Reserve 4-hr window and notify on-call infra 
- Share expected weekday traffic pattern to mirror production bursts

Attachments: MAP_AcmeHealth_v3.pdf, load_script_v2.jmx (please run in non-destructive mode).

If that looks good I’ll ask Marissa to lock in the load window and Rishi to provision scoped test credentials.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance verification and MAP kickoff — results and next steps

Eva/Ben — thank you for a smooth run. Attached: results_20260630.csv (exported from our tracing infra). Summary highlights below (all numbers measured from request -> byte stream under the MAP prompt set):

Summary (steady-state windows):
- 100 concurrent steady-state (30m): p50 token latency 150 ms; p95 token latency 360 ms; sustained aggregate throughput 12.8k tokens/s; TTFT warm 200 ms, TTFT cold 850 ms
- 500 concurrent steady-state (30m): p50 token latency 210 ms; p95 token latency 720 ms; sustained aggregate throughput 58.4k tokens/s; TTFT warm 230 ms, TTFT cold 910 ms
- Error rate observed: 0.03% (transient 429s during second ramp; autoscaler triggered one additional node at 11:12 PST)

Observations / recommendations:
- The platform met our proposed p50/p95 targets at 100 conc; at 500 concurrency p95 is above the aggressive 400 ms target but within the conservative 800 ms target.
- TTFT cold is borderline for some long prompt cases; we recommend keeping a 30–60 minute warm cache policy during production burst windows and enabling prefix caching where applicable.
- Autoscaling was functional — recommend a slightly higher initial pool for planned production production cutovers to limit transient 429s.

Next steps toward close:
1) We’ll update the MAP doc with final numbers and suggested SLA language (target by 2026-07-01 morning).
2) I’ll ask Solutions Engineering to draft a short runbook for production cutover that includes pre-warm steps and autoscaler guardrails.
3) If these results align with your expectations, can we confirm a production pilot start date? Eva — what is your preferred close timeline (targeting July 8 or earlier)?

Attachments: results_20260630.csv (detailed traces), MAP_AcmeHealth_v3.pdf (updated with results).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
